questions.q: The correct statement(s) related to processes involved in the extraction of metals is(are)
options: Copper pyrites is heated with silica in a reverberatory furnace to remove iron
Impure silver is treated with aqueous $KCN$ in the presence of oxygen followed by reduction with zinc metal

Cyanide process, also called Macarthur-forrest Process, method of extracting silver from impure ores by dissolving them in a dilute solution of sodium cyanide in the presence of oxygen. The complex formed in the above process reduced to silver metal by the treatment with zinc.

${O}_{2} + {H}_{2}O + Ag + NaCN\overset{}{\to}Na\left[Ag{\left(CN\right)}_{2}\right] + NaOHNa\left[Ag{\left(CN\right)}_{2}\right]\overset{Zn}{\to}{Na}_{2}\left[Zn{\left(CN\right)}_{4}\right] + Ag$

${SiO}_{2}$​ (Silica) is a flux material. It removes impurities as slag. Here, slag consists of Iron in Sulphide ore of $Cu$, here impurity is $FeO$.

$FeO + {SiO}_{2}\overset{}{\to}{FeSiO}_{3}$

Malachite green is ${CuCO}_{3} . Cu{\left(OH\right)}_{2}$ and cuprite is ${Cu}_{2}O$. The ore malachite green on heating gives cupric oxide but not cuprous oxide.

${CuCO}_{3} . Cu{\left(OH\right)}_{2}\overset{∆}{\to}2CuO + {CO}_{2} + {H}_{2}O$

questions.q: The correct option(s) related to the extraction of iron from its ore in the blast furnace operating in the temperature range $900 - 1500K$ is(are)
options: Limestone is used to remove silicate impurity.
Pig iron obtained from blast furnace contains about $4 %$ carbon.
questions.solution:
(A) Limestone is added to remove silica as impurity.

$CaO + {SiO}_{2} \to {CaSiO}_{3} ( inthetemperaturerange900 – 1500K )$

(B) Pig iron obtained from blast furnace contains $4 %$ carbon and many other impurities (eg. $S, P, Si, Mn$) in small amount.

In fusion zone molten iron becomes heavy by absorbing elemental impurities and produces Pig iron. (in the temperature range 900 – 1500 K)

(C) Coke $\left(C\right)$ converts ${CO}_{2} in CO$.

$C + {CO}_{2} \to 2CO$

(D) Exhaust gases consist of $CO and {CO}_{2}$.

Exhaust gases does not contain NO2

Hence, (A,B,C) are correct.

questions.q: The electrochemical extraction of aluminium from bauxite ore involves
options: the reaction of ${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ with coke $\left(C\right)$ at a temperature $> 2500 ° C$.
the neutralization of aluminate solution by passing ${CO}_{2}$ gas to precipitate hydrated alumina $\left({Al}_{2}{O}_{3} . 3{H}_{2}O\right)$.
the dissolution of ${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ in hot aqueous $NaOH$.
the electrolysis of ${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ mixed with ${Na}_{3}{AlF}_{6}$ to give $Al$ and ${CO}_{2}$.
questions.solution:
(A) The reduction of ${Al}_{2}{O}_{3}$ with coke $\left(C\right)$ at a temperature $> 2500 ° C$ is not carried out due to the formation of carbides.

(B) It is correct as neutralisation of aluminate solution is done by passing ${CO}_{2}$ gas to precipitate hydrated alumina.

(C) Reaction of powdered one is carried out with hot concentrated $NaOH$ at $473K - 523K and 35 - 36$ bar pressure.

(D)Aluminium In the metallurgy of aluminium, purified Al2O3 is mixed with ${Na}_{3}{AlF}_{6}$ or CaF2 which lowers the melting point of the mixture and brings conductivity.Thus electrolysis of the molten mass is carried out in an electrolytic cell using carbon electrodes. The oxygen liberated at anode reacts with the carbon of anode producing CO and CO2 and Al at the cathode.

options:
II, III in haematite and III in magnetite

II, III in haematite and II in magnetite

II in haematite and II, III in magnetite

III in haematite and II, III in magnetite
questions.solution: Haematite is $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$, in which oxidation number of iron is III. Magnetite is $\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4$ which is infact a mixed oxide (FeO $\cdot \mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ ) hence, iron is present in both II and III oxidation state.

questions.q: Extraction of metal from the ore cassiterite involves
options:
carbon reduction of an oxide ore

self-reduction of a sulphide ore

removal of copper impurity

removal of iron impurity
questions.solution:
The important ore of tin is cassiterite $\left(\mathrm{SnO}_2\right)$. Tin is extracted from cassiterite ore by carbon reduction method in a blast furnace. $\mathrm{SnO}_2+2 \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Sn}+2 \mathrm{CO}$
The product often contain traces of iron which is removed by blowing air through the melt to oxidise to $\mathrm{FeO}$ which then floats to the surface.
$2 \mathrm{Fe}+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}$

questions.q: Native silver metal forms a water soluble complex with a dilute aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ in the presence of
questions.solution:
A water soluble complex of silver with a dilute aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ is sodium argentocyanide. In the cyanide process, the native form is crushed and treated with $0.1-0.2 \%$ solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ and aerated.

4 $\mathrm{Ag}+$8 $\mathrm{NaCN}+$2 $\mathrm{H}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}$}_{2} \longrightarrow 4 $\mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_$2\right]+4 $\mathrm{NaOH}$Argentocyanide is soluble. Further, metals are recovered from the complex by reduction with zinc
questions.question: Native silver metal forms a water soluble complex with a dilute aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ in the presence of
questions.explanation:
A water soluble complex of silver with a dilute aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ is sodium argentocyanide. In the cyanide process, the native form is crushed and treated with $0.1-0.2 \%$ solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ and aerated.
$$
4 \mathrm{Ag}+8 \mathrm{NaCN}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+4 \mathrm{NaOH}
$$
Argentocyanide is soluble. Further, metals are recovered from the complex by reduction with zinc

questions.q: Extraction for zinc from zinc blende is achieved by
options:
electrolytic reduction

roasting followed by reduction with carbon

roasting followed by reduction with another metal

roasting followed by self-reduction
questions.solution:
Zinc blende is roasted and then treated with coke for the reduction.

$\begin{gathered}$2 $\mathrm{ZnS}+$3 $\mathrm{O}}_{2} \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2  \mathrm{ZnO}+2  \mathrm{SO}$}_{2} \uparrow \\
$\mathrm{ZnO}+\mathrm{C} \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{CO} \uparrow
\end{gathered}$
questions.question: Extraction for zinc from zinc blende is achieved by
questions.explanation:
Zinc blende is roasted and then treated with coke for the reduction.
$$
\begin{gathered}
2 \mathrm{ZnS}+3 \mathrm{O}_2 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{ZnO}+2 \mathrm{SO}_2 \uparrow \\
\mathrm{ZnO}+\mathrm{C} \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Zn}+\mathrm{CO} \uparrow
\end{gathered}
$$

options:
(A) P,S, (B) R, (C) P,Q, (D) P,S

(A) Q,S, (B) R, (C) S, (D) S

(A) P,R, (B) P, (C) Q, (D) S
questions.solution:
Column I
Column II
(A) Self reduction $\left[$\begin{array}{c}P $\text{ - Lead }$ \\ R $\text{ - Copper }$\end{array}$\right] \begin{aligned}& \text{ i.e., }A \rightleftarrows P \text{ and }R \\
& \text{ In lead metal }\\
& \qquad\left\{$\begin{array}{c}
2 $\mathrm{PbS}+$3 $\mathrm{O}$}_{2} \longrightarrow 2  $\mathrm{PbO}+$2  $\mathrm{SO}$}_{2} \\
2 $\mathrm{PbO}+\mathrm{PbS}$ \longrightarrow3 $\mathrm{ Pb}+\mathrm{SO}_{2}$
\end{array}$\right.
\end{aligned}

(self reduction)
In copper metal

\begin{aligned}& 2 \mathrm{Cu}}_{2} \mathrm{ S}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2  \mathrm{Cu}}_{2} \mathrm{O}+2 \mathrm{SO}_{2} \\
& \mathrm{Cu}}_{2} \mathrm{ S}+2 \mathrm{Cu}_{2}  \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow6  \mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{SO}}_{2}
\end{aligned}

(self reduction)
(B) Carbon reduction $ P$-lead

\begin{aligned}
& \text{ i.e., } \mathrm{B}-\mathrm{P}\\
& \text{ In lead metal }\\
& \qquad \mathrm{PbO}+\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Pb}+\mathrm{CO}\\
& \mathrm{PbO}+\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Pb}+\mathrm{CO}_{2}
\end{aligned}

Carbon reduction process is used for the reduction of oxides of electropositive metals like \mathrm{Fe}, \mathrm{Pb} etc. This reduction is carried out with coal or coke on strongly heating.
(C) Complex formation and displacement by metal.
i.e., $ C-Q$ (silver)

In silver metal
Argentite mineral of \mathrm{Ag} \left(\mathrm{Ag}$}_{2} $\mathrm{ S}\right)$ is treated with $0.7 \% \mathrm{NaCN} solution in presence of air, therefore firstly sodium argento cyanide complex is formed which on heating with zinc metal, therefore by displacement silver is isolated.

\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{Ag}_2  \mathrm{ S}+4  \mathrm{NaCN} \longrightarrow2  \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+ \mathrm{Na}_2  \mathrm{ S}\\
& 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+ \mathrm{Zn} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]+\underset{\text{ Soluble }}{2 \mathrm{Ag}} \downarrow
\end{aligned}

(D) Decomposition of iodide-(S) Boron

\text{ i.e., }(D)-(S)

By decomposition of iodide boron metal is isolated.$
